Compositional data transformation

step_coda.Rd

Transform the selected experiment to centered log-ratio (CLR) or additive log-ratio (ALR) coordinates. By default, glyclean::auto_coda() chooses the transformation.

Usage

step_coda(
  method = "auto",
  by = NULL,
  gamma = 0.1,
  group_scales = NULL,
  seed = 123,
  on = "exp"
)

Arguments

method

Use "auto" (default) for glyclean::auto_coda(), "clr" for glyclean::transform_clr(), or "alr" for glyclean::transform_alr(). Automatic selection uses site-wise CLR for glycoproteomics. For other experiments, it uses CLR for up to 50 features and attempts ALR above 50. The ALR method falls back to CLR if no suitable reference is available. Glycoproteomics supports "auto" and "clr".

by

Either a column name in sample_info or a factor/vector with one value per sample.

gamma

Standard deviation of the scale-uncertainty model on the log2 scale. Default is 0.1. Set to 0 for deterministic transformation.

group_scales

Optional informed group scales. For binary comparisons, this can be a single positive ratio for the second group relative to the first, or two positive scales from which that ratio is derived. For multi-group data, provide a positive vector with one scale per group. All scales and any derived two-group ratio must be finite and strictly positive.

seed

Non-negative integer seed for random number generation. Default is 123. The caller's random state is restored, including on errors.

on

Name of the experiment in the blueprint. Defaults to "exp". For example, use "dynamic_motif_exp" or "branch_motif_exp" after quantifying motifs, then use the same on in the statistical step.

Value

A glysmith_step object.

Details

Place this step after abundance preprocessing and before statistical analysis. The input must contain finite, positive abundances on the raw scale or finite values on a known log scale. A transformation error stops the blueprint so subsequent tests cannot accidentally use the input scale.

The step replaces on with the transformed experiment and saves its previous value in pre_coda_<on> (by default, pre_coda_exp). Subsequent steps targeting the same experiment use its log2-ratio coordinates directly. A successful ALR omits the reference feature from those tests. Use glyclean::get_pipeline() on the output to see which transform ran.

Differential tests return p-values on these coordinates. For example, limma's estimate is the contrast in log2-ratio units. Abundance log2fc is undefined, so significant features are selected by p-value (glystats::filter_sig_vars() ignores an explicit fold-change cutoff with a warning). Volcano plots and fold-change-based protein enrichment are skipped. Run abundance QC, trait derivation, and motif quantification before transforming the main experiment.

Examples

blueprint(step_coda(by = "group", gamma = 0), step_pca(), step_dea_limma())
#> 
#> ── Blueprint (3 steps) ──
#> 
#> • step_coda(by = "group", gamma = 0)
#> • step_pca()
#> • step_dea_limma()
step_coda(method = "clr", gamma = 0)
#> <step "step_coda(method = \"clr\", gamma = 0)"> Compositional data
#> transformation
blueprint(
  step_quantify_branch_motifs(),
  step_coda(on = "branch_motif_exp"),
  step_dea_limma(on = "branch_motif_exp")
)
#> 
#> ── Blueprint (3 steps) ──
#> 
#> • step_quantify_branch_motifs()
#> • step_coda(on = "branch_motif_exp")
#> • step_dea_limma(on = "branch_motif_exp")
